answer: Stake-locked identity registration resists sybil attacks: every agent must lock a token deposit to obtain a working credential, and honest peers can slash deposits attested as fraudulent. An attacker cannot inflate a nebula of cheap fake identities, because each fake must climb the same capital ridge and pay the full stake. When the network detects a grove of identities funded from a single wallet, it raises their required stake, turning mass identity creation into linear capital exhaustion for the attacker.
